start.name: Edfu (Idfu) city, Aswan Governorate, Egypt — GASCO transmission-line delivery point serving two sugar/paper factories and city households
start.coord_basis: Town centroid of Edfu/Idfu, Aswan Governorate — a well-known, independently geocodable Nile-valley town (reused from the prior sweep suggestion; consistent with the town's published location, not read off a map image)

end.name: Unconfirmed — tie-in point on the GASCO South Valley / 'Upper Egypt' gas transmission trunk (Dahshour–Aswan corridor, GEM P0477). Most plausible candidate is a pressure-reduction/metering hub at or near Kom Ombo (independently documented as distributing gas onward to Edfu, Kom Ombo and Nasr al-Nuba villages), or the Aswan terminus itself — the exact valve-room/tie-in location is not stated in any source found
end.coord_basis: No independently geocodable tie-in point identified; do not substitute Kom Ombo town-center coordinates for the actual (unsourced) valve-room location

prior_research.notes: Argaam.com (already GEM's own Status[ref] for this row) independently confirms the GASCO-built 37 km / 12-inch line and states its purpose as delivering gas to 'two sugar and paper factories' and residential Edfu — this corroborates (2nd independent source, alongside Youm7 2022) the prior-suggestion's characterization of Edfu city as the delivery/terminal end. Youm7 (2025) and Elbalad confirm Egypt Gas Company's LOCAL distribution build-out around Edfu/Kom Ombo/Nasr al-Nuba markaz (a different infrastructure layer — low-pressure household/industrial distribution fed off this GASCO transmission spur), which is consistent with, but does not itself pin down, the transmission-line trunk tie-in. I could not find any source (Arabic or English) that names the specific valve-room or km-point where the 37 km line leaves the Dahshour–Aswan ('Upper Egypt') trunk — Kom Ombo is the best-supported bounding candidate (documented pressure-reduction/metering hub in that corridor) but is NOT itself confirmed as the tie-in, and Kom Ombo–Edfu is only ~15–20 km by road versus the sheet's 37 km, so treat 'near Kom Ombo' as a loose bound, not a fix. Recommend leaving this at ROUTE_PARTIAL (corridor-only, no two-point candidate) pending a GASCO network map or tender document naming the tie-in station explicitly. RouteAccuracy should stay capped at 'low' per the source ladder rules.

prior_research.notes: Could not source this specific 27km 'Fayoum-Giza Gas Pipeline.' Ruled out: it is NOT one of the three lines in Ministry of Petroleum Decree 1884/2025 (those total 40.5km across Beni Suef-New Fayoum/19km, Fayoum-expansion-support/12km, and Itsa-supply/9.5km -- all already accounted for as P6686/P8012/P8011, none named Giza); and it is NOT the Solaimaneyah-North Giza line (Decree 1883/2025, 20km, a different corridor through Giza/Monufia governorates along the Regional Ring Road -- that is P6685). Searched English and Arabic (خط غاز الفيوم الجيزة, GASCO/EGAS project pages, Egyptian press, official-gazette search) with no hit on a discrete decree, GASCO project page, or news item describing a 27km Fayoum-to-Giza gas line. gem.wiki has no page yet for this pipeline (blank), so no internal lead there either. Speculative/unsourced corridor guess only: given the naming convention (GASCO/Ministry lines are routinely named '<place A>-<place B>'), this is plausibly a link between the Fayoum distribution network (e.g. the Fayoum-Giza desert road corridor near Demu/New Fayoum City, see P8012's start) and a point in rural Giza Governorate's Nile-valley markaz (Atfih/Badrashin/El-Saff), which would roughly fit a 27km span -- but this is not sourced and should not be treated as more than a hypothesis for a follow-up search (e.g. querying the Egyptian Official Gazette portal directly, or GASCO/EGAS annual reports, for a 'Fayoum-Giza' or similarly named decree).

start.name: Zaafarana (Za'faranah), Gulf of Suez coast, Red Sea Governorate
start.coord_basis: OSM/Nominatim geocode of 'زعفرانة' (Zaafarana locality), Red Sea Governorate.

end.name: El Kureimat power station complex
end.coord_basis: OSM/Nominatim geocode of 'قرية الكريمات' (Kureimat village), Giza Governorate — same anchor used for P8021.

prior_research.notes: Kureimat endpoint is well-sourced (see P8021 notes); Zaafarana's location is confirmed by public geocoding but I found NO public source describing a gas pipeline export FROM Zaafarana to Kureimat specifically — the only Zaafarana gas-pipeline hits were unrelated: a short GEMPETCO offshore-to-onshore field pipeline at Zaafarana (elmostqpalelyuom.com/34335, ~18km, 4in — a different, much smaller project, do not conflate) and a PMS efficiency project (nabd.com) on the same offshore field. Notable lead: a real, named, mapped road — 'طريق الزعفرانة - الكريمات' (Zaafarana–Kureimat Road, per Wikimapia listings) — runs exactly this Gulf-of-Suez-to-Nile-Valley corridor across the Eastern Desert, ~89km from Suez per one Wikimapia entry (consistent with, though shorter than, the sheet's 163km total, which would include the Nile-valley leg down to Kureimat). Egyptian gas trunks are frequently laid parallel to such roads (as independently confirmed for P7574's Sokhna–Cairo Road corridor), so this is a plausible corridor, but NOT a sourced pipeline claim — marking resolved:false rather than guessing. Recommend flagging for a follow-up search once WebSearch quota resets (try GASCO route maps or Arabic press specifically on this corridor).
